key_insight: The paper shows that recovering an ODE from solution trajectories can be framed as a geometric identifiability problem using Hausdorff distance between solution sets, yielding conditions for when the true governing equation is uniquely and stably recoverable.
engineering_relevance: This provides a theory-driven basis for deciding how many trajectories are needed to learn dynamics reliably in scientific machine learning, system identification, and data-driven model discovery.
method: Defines a Hausdorff-distance metric on sets of ODE solutions to compare candidate governing equations.
Derives identifiability bounds for linear ODEs and nonlinear ODE classes with Lipschitz/Hölder-continuous vector fields.
Uses metric entropy arguments to estimate sample complexity for recovering the governing equation from multiple solution observations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical identifiability and metric-entropy/sample-complexity analysis across classes of ODEs, but does not mention a numerical benchmark or experimental dataset.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on the chosen ODE class and assumptions such as solution observability and regularity of the vector field, so practical recovery may weaken under noise, sparse trajectories, or model misspecification.
paper_title: Recovering Governing Equations from Solution Data: Identifiability Bounds for Linear and Nonlinear ODEs
